This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #48026
* #48025
* #48024

* #48004
* #48003
* #48002
* #48001

## Motivation

Unified memory reclaimed through a stack of per-shape protocols (a FULL cache donor for state slots, per-shape reclaim plans, the prefix tree's per-component targets), and capacity reads used per-band views and the sizing's static per-side split. Both disagreed with what a take could actually serve: capacity reads missed room that compacting an end or moving a float opens, could report free state ids no layout could place, and a decode preallocation could pass separate state and token checks and still fail its take.

## Modifications

- One victim loop (`mem_cache/kv/alloc/chain.py`, `unified_radix_cache.py`): if the demand fits (relayout allowed), take it; if it would not fit even with every evictable entry evicted, evict nothing; otherwise evict victims in the cache's order one at a time, checking the fit after each and stopping at the first fit. Admission credits the same evictable entries (`admits`). The donor protocol and the per-shape reclaim plans are removed.
- Decode preallocation prices a request's pending state slots together with its tokens in one question (`disaggregation/decode.py`, `allocator/{base,swa,hisparse}.py`).
- Capacity reads (`chain.py`, `kv/storage.py`, `unified_memory_pool.py`, `managers/scheduler_components/pool_stats_observer.py`): a sub-pool's availability is the largest demand of that sub-pool alone a take can serve now; the token read is the largest demand the owner and every window can take together. Sub-pools share bytes, so availabilities do not add up.
- The per-shape capacity policies, pricing functions, credited reservation check and float movers are removed (`kv/alloc/interim.py`, `pricing.py`, `band.py`); a float moves only by `relocate_into`. A relief first lays the chain out with rows under unfinished network transfers held in place; only when no such layout serves the demand does it fall back and wait on the host for those transfers. Bands' neighbour-credit capacity read is removed.
- Tests: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_reclaim_victim_loop.py`, `test_unified_move_destinations.py`, `test_unified_state_usage.py`, plus planner-question rewrites of the pricing, tri-pool, joint-reclaim and HiCache tests; `test_unified_dynamic_gate_capacity.py` is removed with the policy it tested.

**Observable change (unified memory only):** reported available sizes and usage come from the layout planner, so they can be larger than before (room a rearrangement opens) and per-sub-pool availabilities overlap. State usage is reported as 0 when no state slot is held and other sub-pools hold the bytes.

## Accuracy Tests

Serving validation was run at the **top of this 26-PR stack** (the cumulative change), not at this PR's head. Software: torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10. GSM8K is few-shot, 500 or 1319 questions as noted; `main` is the same commit the stack is based on, same flags.

| Hardware | Model | Configuration | Stack top | main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, `--enable-unified-memory` (rebased stack) | 0.954 (1319 q) | 0.950–0.954 |
| 1x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP1, `--enable-unified-memory --max-total-tokens 120000` (rebased stack) | 0.842 (1319 q) | 0.839 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, MTP (EAGLE, 3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens) | 0.951, accept length 3.56 | 0.953, 3.56 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, DFlash draft | 0.951, accept length 5.42 | 0.952, 5.44 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | PD (prefill TP1 + decode TP1, mooncake), unified, repeated runs | 0.952–0.960, no hang | 0.954–0.958 |
| 2x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | PD (TP1 + TP1, mooncake), unified | 0.810 | 0.808 |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified, HiCache | 0.954 | — |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | PP2, unified | 0.953 | 0.955 (static pools) |
| 2x B200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B | TP2, unified (500 q) | 0.958 | 0.960 |
| 2x B200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP2, unified, `trtllm_mha` (1319 q) | 0.849 | 0.863 |
| 2x B300 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B / openai/gpt-oss-120b | TP2, unified | 0.950 / 0.849 | 0.954 / 0.849 |

On B200 and B300, 40 greedy GSM8K generations were compared with `main`: 35–40 of 40 are identical, and the rest first differ after at least 27 characters (near ties). The H200 runs above other than the two marked "rebased stack" were run at the stack top before it was rebased onto the current base; the code they cover is unchanged by the rebase except for conflict resolutions.

Every unified row exercises the victim loop and the planner's capacity reads.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured at the stack top, same flags as `main` (bench_serving, random 4096-in / 512-out unless noted):

| Hardware | Model / configuration | Stack top | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b, unified, `--max-total-tokens 120000` | 3.93–3.95 req/s | 3.95 req/s |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B PD (TP1 + TP1), 2048-in / 256-out | 5.65–6.28 req/s | 6.21–6.29 req/s |
| 2x H200 | openai/gpt-oss-120b PD (TP1 + TP1) | 9.39–9.45 req/s | 9.21 req/s |
| 2x H200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B MTP TP2 / DFlash TP2 | 4.26 / 4.36 req/s | 4.29 / 4.35 req/s |
| 2x B200 | Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B TP2 / openai/gpt-oss-120b TP2 | 6.35 / 19.31 req/s | 6.34 / 19.28 req/s |

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

         *,

         swa_budget_tokens: int | None = None,
+        state_slots: int = 0,
     ) -> bool:
         """Whether a decode-node preallocation of this size fits.
 
         The budgets are the scheduler's policy: what each side has left once
         decode headroom and retraction are reserved. Separate buffers make the
         two sides independent, so each is checked against its own budget and

+"""What a page move may overwrite, and what it may wait for.
+
+A request's row can go back to the free list while a forward launched before
+the release still writes its next slot (an overlapped batch): a copy into that
+hole must wait the forward. A row a network peer reads or writes is moved only
+when no other layout serves the allocation, since moving it waits on the host
+until the peer is done. A relief reads everything it needs on the host before
+its first stream wait.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.alloc.chain import ChainAllocator, ChainRoles
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.alloc.signals import NetworkTransfer
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+from sglang.test.unified_allocator_fixtures import (
+    FakeKVCache,
+    FakeUnifiedSWAKVPool,
+    arena_of,
+    setup_allocator_context,
+    stand_in_views,
+    tri_sub_pool_specs,
+)
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=12, stage="extra-a", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+_ROLES = ChainRoles(owner="full", window="swa", state="mamba")
+
+
+class _Chain(CustomTestCase):
+    def _chain(self, tokens):
+        setup_allocator_context()
+        full, swa, mamba = tri_sub_pool_specs(head_num=1, head_dim=8)
+        pool = arena_of(
+            total_bytes=48 * full.entry_bytes()
+            + 32 * swa.entry_bytes()
+            + 8 * mamba.entry_bytes(),
+            sub_pool_specs=[full, swa, mamba],
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        kvcache = FakeUnifiedSWAKVPool(pool)
+        state = FakeKVCache(pool, "mamba")
+        for fake in (kvcache.full_kv_pool, kvcache.swa_kv_pool, state):
+            fake.buf = fake.buf.cuda()
+        alloc = ChainAllocator(
+            roles=_ROLES,
+            arena=pool,
+            kvcache=kvcache,
+            views=stand_in_views(_ROLES, kvcache, state),
+            device="cuda",
+            full_max_total_num_tokens=48,
+            swa_max_total_num_tokens=32,
+            need_sort=False,
+            forward_stream=None,
+            lazy_compaction=True,
+        )
+        ids = alloc.alloc(tokens)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(ids)
+        schedule, side = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
+        with torch.cuda.stream(schedule):
+            # A running scheduler has loaded these kernels and pinned buffers.
+            for band in alloc.members:
+                band.prewarm_compaction()
+                band._to_device([0])
+                for part in (ids[:1], ids[1:2], ids[:10], ids):

+class TestReliefsAroundNetworkRows(_Chain):
+    """The owner's end holds a row a network peer touches near its frontier

+    def _owner_with_holes(self):

+        phys = full.ids.virtual_to_physical[ids].tolist()
+        by_page = {p: ids[i : i + 1] for i, p in enumerate(phys)}
+        low = min(phys)

+        row_page = low + 2
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        return pool, alloc, full, by_page[row_page], row_page, schedule, side

+    def _waiter(self, alloc, done=None):
+        """A network waiter standing in for the engine: it records each wait
+        and returns once ``done`` (the engine's last touch) fired."""
+        calls = []
+
+        def wait(transfers):
+            calls.append([t.peer for t in transfers])
+            if done is not None:
+                done.synchronize()
+
+        alloc.set_network_waiter(wait)
+        return calls

+    def _record(self, full, page, peer, *, writes):
+        transfer = NetworkTransfer(peer)

+            [page],

+            unit_tokens=full.pool_page_size,
+        )
+        return transfer

+            laid = torch.cuda.Event()
+            laid.record()
+        return laid

+        serves the allocation around the row, the row stays where it is and
+        nothing waits for the receive."""

+        calls = self._waiter(alloc)

+"""Reclaim on unified memory: victims one at a time in the cache's order,
+every walk stopping at the first victim after which the demand fits."""
+
+import random
+import unittest
+from array import array
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import (
+    EvictParams,
+    InsertParams,
+    MatchPrefixParams,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.alloc.pricing import first_plan
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.radix_cache import RadixKey
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.component_type import ComponentType
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import reset_context
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+from sglang.test.unified_allocator_fixtures import (
+    build_tri_cache,
+    setup_allocator_context,
+)
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=20, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _evictable(cache):
+    return (
+        cache.full_evictable_size(),
+        cache.swa_evictable_size(),
+        cache.mamba_evictable_size(),
+    )
+
+
+class TestReclaimVictimLoop(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.addCleanup(reset_context)
+        setup_allocator_context()
+
+    def _cache_prefixes(self, rng, allocator, cache, state_slots, count, lock):
+        """``count`` cached prefixes, each with its state checkpoint, a share of
+        them locked as running requests lock their prefixes."""
+        receipts = []
+        states = []
+        while len(states) < count:
+            state = state_slots.alloc(1)
+            if state is None:
+                break
+            states.append(state.reshape(1))
+        for i, state in enumerate(states):
+            length = rng.randint(1, 8)
+            tokens = allocator.alloc(length)
+            if tokens is None:
+                # Out of room: the states left stay with running requests.
+                break
+            key = RadixKey(array("q", range(i * 1000, i * 1000 + length)))
+            cache.insert(InsertParams(key=key, value=tokens, mamba_value=state))
+            if rng.random() < lock:
+                node = cache.match_prefix(MatchPrefixParams(key=key)).last_device_node
+                receipts.append(
+                    (
+                        node,
+                        cache.inc_lock_ref(
+                            node, skip_lock_components=(ComponentType.MAMBA,)
+                        ),
+                    )
+                )
+        return receipts
+
+    def test_short_owner_is_walked_first(self):
+        # The owner alone is short: its own cached entries are the first
+        # victims, and the walk stops at the first one after which the demand
+        # fits (rearranged if need be), long before its cache is gone.
+        for lazy in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(lazy=lazy):
+                rng = random.Random(7)
+                bundle, allocator, cache = build_tri_cache(lazy=lazy)
+                state_slots = bundle.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.state_slots
+                self._cache_prefixes(rng, allocator, cache, state_slots, 6, 0.0)
+                # Running requests fill the owner; their windows have retired.
+                while allocator.ensure_capacity(4, 4):
+                    allocator.free_swa(allocator.alloc(4))
+                owner = allocator.full_attn_allocator.sub_pool_name
+                demand = {owner: allocator.full_available_size() + 2}
+                self.assertFalse(allocator._units_fit(demand))
+                walks = []
+                original = cache.evict_for_alloc
+
+                def walk(params, **kwargs):
+                    result = original(params, **kwargs)
+                    walks.append((params, result))
+                    return result
+
+                with patch.object(cache, "evict_for_alloc", side_effect=walk):
+                    self.assertTrue(allocator.reclaim(cache, demand))
+                first = walks[0][0]
+                self.assertGreater(first.num_tokens, 0)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    (
+                        first.swa_num_tokens,
+                        first.auxiliary_swa_num_tokens,
+                        first.mamba_num,
+                    ),
+                    (0, 0, 0),
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(len(walks), 1)
+                self.assertLess(walks[0][1].num_tokens_evicted, first.num_tokens)
+                self.assertTrue(allocator._units_fit(demand))
+                self.assertIsNotNone(
+                    allocator.realize(first_plan(allocator.pricing_snapshot(), demand))
+                )
+                self.assertFalse(allocator.verify_byte_accounting())
+
+    def _history(self, rng):
+        bundle, allocator, cache = build_tri_cache(lazy=rng.random() < 0.5)
+        state_slots = bundle.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.state_slots
+        count = rng.randint(1, max(1, state_slots.available_size() - 3))
+        receipts = self._cache_prefixes(rng, allocator, cache, state_slots, count, 0.3)
+        # Running requests hold the rest of the token room.
+        while rng.random() < 0.8 and allocator.ensure_capacity(4, 4):
+            self.assertIsNotNone(allocator.alloc(4))
+        return allocator, cache, receipts
+
+    def test_admitted_demand_is_reclaimed_and_taken(self):
+        # Admission credits every evictable entry; the reclaim the take runs
+        # first realizes that credit; a demand admission refuses evicts
+        # nothing, so the caller refuses or retracts with the cache intact.
+        rng = random.Random(20261031)
+        outcomes = set()
+        for seed in range(200):
+            with self.subTest(seed=seed):
+                allocator, cache, receipts = self._history(rng)
+                tokens = rng.randint(1, 48)
+                slots = rng.randint(0, 2)
+                admitted = allocator.admits(
+                    tokens,
+                    allocator._window_demand(tokens, tokens),
+                    slots,
+                    evictable=allocator.admission_evictable(cache),
+                )
+                before = _evictable(cache)
+                ready = allocator.reclaim(
+                    cache, allocator.page_demands(tokens, tokens, state_slots=slots)
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(ready, admitted)
+                outcomes.add(admitted)
+                if not admitted:
+                    self.assertEqual(_evictable(cache), before)
+                else:
+                    if slots:
+                        self.assertIsNotNone(allocator.alloc_state_slots(slots))
+                    self.assertIsNotNone(allocator.alloc(tokens))
+                self.assertFalse(allocator.verify_byte_accounting())
+                for node, receipt in receipts:
+                    cache.dec_lock_ref(node, receipt.to_dec_params())
+        self.assertEqual(outcomes, {False, True})
+
+    def test_component_shortfall_reclaims_the_demand(self):
+        # Callers that make room for one component's take name its shortfall
+        # against that component's capacity read (the state slot check before
+        # binding a request, a host load's device rows). On unified memory the
+        # shortfall is the component's demand less its read, so the reclaim
+        # answers exactly as the demand's own admission and reclaim do.
+        rng = random.Random(20261101)
+        outcomes = set()
+        for seed in range(150):
+            with self.subTest(seed=seed):
+                allocator, cache, receipts = self._history(rng)
+                owner = allocator.full_attn_allocator.sub_pool_name
+                window = allocator.swa_attn_allocator.sub_pool_name
+                state = allocator.mamba_allocator.sub_pool_name
+                component = rng.choice(("owner", "window", "state"))
+                if component == "state":
+                    need = rng.randint(1, 3)
+                    read = allocator.state_slots_available()
+                    params = EvictParams(mamba_num=need - read)
+                    demand = {state: need}
+                    admitted = allocator.admits(
+                        0,
+                        {},
+                        need,
+                        evictable=allocator.admission_evictable(cache),
+                    )
+                else:
+                    page = allocator.page_size
+                    need = rng.randint(1, 48)
+                    name = owner if component == "owner" else window
+                    read = allocator.units_available(name)
+                    if component == "owner":
+                        params = EvictParams(num_tokens=need - read)
+                    else:
+                        params = EvictParams(swa_num_tokens=need - read)
+                    demand = {name: -(-need // page)}
+                    admitted = allocator.admits(
+                        need if component == "owner" else 0,
+                        {} if component == "owner" else {window: need},
+                        evictable=allocator.admission_evictable(cache),
+                    )
+                before = _evictable(cache)
+                if need > read:
+                    cache.evict_for_alloc(params)
+                self.assertEqual(allocator._units_fit(demand), admitted)
+                outcomes.add(admitted)
+                if not admitted:
+                    self.assertEqual(_evictable(cache), before)
+                elif component == "state":
+                    self.assertIsNotNone(allocator.alloc_state_slots(need))
+                self.assertFalse(allocator.verify_byte_accounting())
+                for node, receipt in receipts:
+                    cache.dec_lock_ref(node, receipt.to_dec_params())
+        self.assertEqual(outcomes, {False, True})
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+    def test_held_plus_available_when_state_ids_outnumber_their_bytes(self):

+        # Fill the token sub-pool until it holds bytes a free state id maps to:
+        # then that id is free but no take can place it.
+        while allocator.state_slots_available() >= state.available_size():
+            if allocator.alloc(allocator.page_size) is None:
+                break

+
+        usage = self._state_usage(storage)
